summary: Related pack (features cli/verify/client/server/lattice; claims 67609c19-de05-862c-8db7-e5dc95f38cee..004/007/008; 628207d3-7b88-880b-abe1-acd523f8572f/016; docs consumer-cli + work-model/vision; worktree scan caution-only) shows the bet aims right (full init + installable bin + Release→npm for alpha) but cannot seal yet: skeleton contract is untestable (tenets vs 628207d3-7b88-880b-abe1-acd523f8572f drift), UI path is OR-shaped atop private+file:@nessa-ui, workspace:* publishability not acceptance-bound, ee4b88b6-f54b-8011-82e1-e4d44b94aaab mega-claim fuses 7274f0f7-06fc-809b-bf50-34149f1a028d/03/04, expectedPaths missing under requireAlignApprove, and NPM_TOKEN publish lacks negative/security acceptance despite securitySensitive:false. Graph feature cli has empty claimIds and entryPoints only main+init — understates .github/workflows + client/server/ui pack surface.
plainSummary: Seal is blocked: init, Lattice publish, and Release→npm rules are still too vague for a consumer to get a trustworthy install path.
residualRisks: worktrees.scanned caution-only string from related pack — not a seal blocker; authority remains this checkout

Proposed killers (post-amend): K-init-skeleton-list (fixture dir/file set after init); K-init-no-pass (verify after init invents no claim/binding pass); K-pack-bin (tarball install outside monorepo runs --help/init/verify); K-pack-client-server (no workspace: in packed package.json; install resolves); K-ui-path (chosen publish OR artifact path succeeds without file:../../../nessa); K-release-trigger (workflow yaml on: release only; push/PR job cannot publish); K-version-tag (published version matches Release tag / alpha line)

findings.gap: Acceptance and 628207d3-7b88-880b-abe1-acd523f8572f say 'contracted full skeleton' / 'stub or empty dirs as documented' but there is no normative, machine-checkable file/dir list. Pitch prose includes tenets; 628207d3-7b88-880b-abe1-acd523f8572f and d1be55a6-11bb-8460-8650-ddf0ecac8185.acceptanceCriteria omit tenets; themes/vision/reviews/proposed-claims/workstreams listed inconsistently. Current initLedger only creates claims/bindings/graph/policy/results/turns — delta is large and untestable without a fixture contract.
findings.plainImpact: Two agents could ship different init layouts and both claim the skeleton is done.
findings.fixProposal: Add a sealed appendix or attachment: exact paths created (files vs empty dirs vs stubs), including whether tenets/ and vision.json|md are required. Point 628207d3-7b88-880b-abe1-acd523f8572f and 141476c9-8a75-8ee1-8eb6-54aa420d3a07 acceptance at that list; add an integration fixture that asserts the set. Drop weasel 'as contracted/as documented' without the document.

findings.gap: 4a65c48e-eaf5-8e43-b1b6-4c7bc8c793ca/ee4b88b6-f54b-8011-82e1-e4d44b94aaab accept 'UI publishable OR Release-artifact runnable' while packages/ui is private:true and depends on @nessa-ui/react via file:../../../nessa/packages/react plus client via file:../client. Rabbit hole acknowledges the link but out-of-scope forbids replacing the design system and allows 'document temporary constraint' — so the consumer Lattice objective can forever defer. Related feature lattice + prior UI turns show this is the product surface, not optional polish.
findings.plainImpact: Consumers could install the CLI and still have no way to see their ledger in Lattice.
findings.fixProposal: Pick one path before seal: (A) publish @nessa/spec-ledger-ui with pinned public @nessa-ui/react (or vendored CSS-only subset) and workspace-stripped client dep; or (B) ship a Release-attached runnable artifact (documented one-liner) and demote npm UI from ee4b88b6-f54b-8011-82e1-e4d44b94aaab. Elevate the chosen path into 4a65c48e-eaf5-8e43-b1b6-4c7bc8c793ca acceptance; remove the OR. Do not treat 'document rabbit hole' as done.

findings.gap: Acceptance mentions publishConfig/files/workspace deps resolved for npm, but client and server package.json use workspace:* and have no files/publishConfig; UI uses file: deps. 7274f0f7-06fc-809b-bf50-34149f1a028d only packs @nessa/spec-ledger; 4a65c48e-eaf5-8e43-b1b6-4c7bc8c793ca says 'npm-publishable' without a pack-install oracle. Pack-time workspace stripping is rabbit-hole prose, not acceptance.
findings.plainImpact: Published client or server packages could be uninstallable outside this monorepo.
findings.fixProposal: Per package in 7274f0f7-06fc-809b-bf50-34149f1a028d/03: after pnpm pack (or documented publish dry-run), packed package.json must contain no workspace: or file: protocol deps; files/exports must include runnable dist (+ bin for ledger/server). Add integration evidence installing client+server tarballs against a packed ledger version.

findings.gap: ee4b88b6-f54b-8011-82e1-e4d44b94aaab is a mega-claim: installable bin + client + server + Lattice UI/artifact + Release-only publish trigger. 7274f0f7-06fc-809b-bf50-34149f1a028d, 4a65c48e-eaf5-8e43-b1b6-4c7bc8c793ca, and 6f2b8a6c-e341-8ca2-84c4-d4427e03529a all cite only ee4b88b6-f54b-8011-82e1-e4d44b94aaab. That fuses mechanism (pack/bin), product surface (Lattice), and CI policy (workflow triggers) — cheap-to-change smell; one failing vertical cannot falsify a clear claim slice.
findings.plainImpact: A partial ship could claim the publish story done while one package or the workflow still fails consumers.
findings.fixProposal: Split proposed claims before seal: e.g. 628207d3-7b88-880b-abe1-acd523f8572f init; ee4b88b6-f54b-8011-82e1-e4d44b94aaab installable ledger bin (+ optional client/server pack); 29a5b902-b969-823e-86f5-89b23debe467 Release→npm trigger + package set / UI artifact. Re-map suggestedSlices proposedClaimIds. Keep each vertical independently fail-able.

findings.gap: policy.requireAlignApprove is true but no suggestedSlices.expectedPaths despite schemas/workstream.json supporting them (76451749-a54f-8579-96f2-dcec19d79026 lesson). Related blast spans packages/ledger (cli), client, server, ui, and net-new .github/workflows publish; graph feature cli entryPoints are only main.ts+init.ts with claimIds:[]. Align coverage will be ad-hoc.
findings.plainImpact: Path coverage could pass or fail arbitrarily because the sealed plan never named allowed files.
findings.fixProposal: Add expectedPaths per slice, e.g. 141476c9-8a75-8ee1-8eb6-54aa420d3a07 packages/ledger/src/cli/**; 7274f0f7-06fc-809b-bf50-34149f1a028d packages/ledger/package.json + bin surface; 4a65c48e-eaf5-8e43-b1b6-4c7bc8c793ca packages/{client,server,ui}/**; 6f2b8a6c-e341-8ca2-84c4-d4427e03529a .github/workflows/** + docs. Optionally extend graph cli entryPoints / locators for workflow + pack scripts.

findings.gap: trust.securitySensitive is false while 6f2b8a6c-e341-8ca2-84c4-d4427e03529a introduces NPM_TOKEN and publish-on-Release — a supply-chain / secret boundary. Acceptance lacks negatives: push/PR must not publish; tag/version mismatch refuses publish; partial multi-package publish failure behavior; dry-run vs live gates; who may cut the first alpha Release. Related pack includes no prior publish workflow (only ci.yml on push/PR).
findings.plainImpact: A mistaken push or tag could publish broken or inconsistent packages to npm.
findings.fixProposal: Either set securitySensitive:true with required evidence for workflow negatives, or keep false but put explicit acceptance + killers: workflow on: [release] (and optional workflow_dispatch dry-run) only; no npm publish step on push/PR; version must equal release tag; document NPM_TOKEN least privilege. Name the workflow file path in acceptance.

findings.gap: Packages are version 0.1.0 today; acceptance allows '0.1.0-alpha.0 or agreed tag' and 'no Release cut unless explicitly creating 0.1.0-alpha'. Weasel 'or agreed' plus undefined 'production Release' vs alpha makes done-ness for 6f2b8a6c-e341-8ca2-84c4-d4427e03529a unclear (workflow merged + dry-run only? or first alpha publish required?).
findings.plainImpact: The team could disagree whether shipping the workflow alone finishes the bet.
findings.fixProposal: Pin the alpha version string in acceptance (e.g. 0.1.0-alpha.0). State explicitly: this bet completes with workflow+docs+dry-run evidence; cutting the GitHub Release is optional human action outside acceptance unless chosen.

findings.gap: Missing init failure modes: re-init on existing ledger.json (today throws); crash mid-write leaving partial tree; init outside a git repo (findRepoRoot falls back to cwd); whether schemas/ must exist for consumer verify/server schema routes (ledger npm files[] is only dist+README — schemas stay in monorepo). No acceptance for these.
findings.plainImpact: Init could leave a half-written ledger or a consumer install that cannot load schemas the tools expect.
findings.fixProposal: Add 141476c9-8a75-8ee1-8eb6-54aa420d3a07 negatives: re-init is refused without clobber; specify git requirement; decide schemas strategy (bundle in package, generate stubs, or document monorepo-only) and put it in acceptance/outOfScope explicitly.

findings.gap: Bet correctly requires not weakening 67609c19-de05-862c-8db7-e5dc95f38cee/2884eafb-114e-85f1-ae07-ce1fbd140550, but acceptance is aspirational. 141476c9-8a75-8ee1-8eb6-54aa420d3a07 says verify runs and does not invent pass without a concrete oracle (empty claims → report shape; no binding status:pass; no stub claims with outcomes). expectedClaimIds include 67609c19-de05-862c-8db7-e5dc95f38cee but not 2884eafb-114e-85f1-ae07-ce1fbd140550 though bindings are in the skeleton.
findings.plainImpact: Init could add stub files that quietly teach verify to look greener than the empty ledger is.
findings.fixProposal: Name the oracle: after init, verify exits with no invented claim pass; bindings dir empty or stubs validate against schemas/binding.json with no status field; cite 2884eafb-114e-85f1-ae07-ce1fbd140550 on 141476c9-8a75-8ee1-8eb6-54aa420d3a07 expectedClaimIds. Killer test in code-break later.

findings.gap: Appetite 1–2 days for full init rewrite + four publish surfaces + @nessa-ui unblock + new Release workflow is under-scoped relative to rabbit holes. 6f2b8a6c-e341-8ca2-84c4-d4427e03529a is largely a horizontal CI chore fused into the same bet as product verticals — risk of shipping workflow theater before consumer pack works.
findings.plainImpact: The bet may seal a schedule that forces shallow publish wiring and leaves consumers broken.
findings.fixProposal: Either extend appetite / cut UI to a follow-on workstream after CLI+client+server pack works, or make 4a65c48e-eaf5-8e43-b1b6-4c7bc8c793ca explicitly optional/follow-on in outOfScope with objective narrowed. Prefer sequencing: 141476c9-8a75-8ee1-8eb6-54aa420d3a07→02→04 for ledger bin, then 4a65c48e-eaf5-8e43-b1b6-4c7bc8c793ca.
